Neural tube defects as a direct consequence of meconium exposure
Meconium aspiration syndrome, causing airway obstruction and chemical pneumonitis in the newborn
Hypospadias as a direct consequence of meconium exposure
obstetrics-and-gynecology/obstetric-comp.e: Meconium-stained amniotic fluid raises concern for meconium aspiration syndrome if the fetus aspirates the meconium-stained fluid before or during delivery, causing airway obstruction, chemical pneumonitis, and impaired gas exchange in the newborn.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/obstetric-comp.s: A category III (abnormal) fetal heart rate tracing, indicating a non-reassuring fetal status, is characterized by which finding?
o: Normal baseline variability with no decelerations
The presence of accelerations only, with normal variability
Absent baseline fetal heart rate variability with recurrent late or variable decelerations, or a sinusoidal pattern
A completely normal baseline heart rate with occasional early decelerations
Moderate variability with no decelerations of any kind
obstetrics-and-gynecology/obstetric-comp.e: A category III fetal heart rate tracing is characterized by absent baseline variability combined with recurrent late or variable decelerations or bradycardia, or a sinusoidal pattern, indicating a high likelihood of abnormal fetal acid-base status and often warranting expedited delivery.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/obstetric-comp.s: Induction of labor using prostaglandin analogues (e.g., misoprostol or dinoprostone) acts primarily by which mechanism?
o: Promoting cervical ripening and stimulating uterine contractions
Directly increasing maternal blood pressure to induce labor
Reducing maternal oxytocin receptor sensitivity
Inhibiting uterine contractions to delay delivery
Directly maturing fetal lungs, similarly to corticosteroids
obstetrics-and-gynecology/obstetric-comp.e: Prostaglandin analogues used for labor induction promote cervical ripening (softening and effacement of the cervix) and stimulate myometrial contractions, facilitating progression toward vaginal delivery in women with an unfavorable cervix.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/obstetric-comp.s: A Bishop score is used clinically to assess which aspect of the maternal cervix prior to induction of labor?
o: The presence or absence of cervical cancer
The degree of cervical incompetence in a non-pregnant patient
The risk of postpartum hemorrhage
Cervical favorability (readiness) for induction, based on dilation, effacement, station, consistency, and position
The likelihood of a multiple gestation
obstetrics-and-gynecology/obstetric-comp.e: The Bishop score assesses cervical favorability for labor induction based on five parameters (cervical dilation, effacement, station of the presenting part, consistency, and position), with a higher score indicating a more favorable cervix and higher likelihood of successful induction.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/obstetric-comp.s: Retained products of conception after delivery are a recognized cause of postpartum hemorrhage and are best confirmed by which investigation?
o: Chest X-ray as the investigation of choice
Serum beta-hCG trend alone, without any imaging
Colposcopy as the investigation of choice
Pelvic ultrasound
Hysterosalpingography performed immediately postpartum
obstetrics-and-gynecology/obstetric-comp.e: Pelvic ultrasound is used to assess for retained products of conception in a woman with ongoing or delayed postpartum bleeding, helping to guide the decision for surgical evacuation if retained tissue is identified.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/obstetric-comp.s: A woman with a prior uterine scar attempting a trial of labor after cesarean should ideally be monitored in which setting?
o: At home without any facility-based monitoring
A facility with continuous fetal monitoring and immediate access to emergency cesarean delivery
In a birthing center with no surgical capability and significant transfer time to a hospital
Under general anesthesia throughout the entire labor
Without any fetal heart rate monitoring, since it is unnecessary in this scenario
obstetrics-and-gynecology/obstetric-comp.e: A trial of labor after cesarean carries a risk of uterine rupture, so it should be conducted in a facility capable of continuous fetal monitoring and immediate emergency cesarean delivery should complications arise.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/obstetric-comp.s: Instrumental delivery using vacuum extraction carries a specific risk of which neonatal complication, related to the suction cup application?
o: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia as a direct result of vacuum application
Cephalohematoma or, less commonly, subgaleal hemorrhage
Meconium aspiration syndrome as a direct result of vacuum application
Neural tube defects as a direct result of vacuum application
Hypospadias as a direct result of vacuum application
obstetrics-and-gynecology/obstetric-comp.e: Vacuum-assisted delivery carries a risk of scalp trauma including cephalohematoma (subperiosteal hemorrhage) and, less commonly but more seriously, subgaleal hemorrhage, related to the suction and traction applied to the fetal scalp.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/obstetric-comp.s: A category II fetal heart rate tracing, an indeterminate pattern, generally warrants which management approach?
o: Continued close monitoring with intrauterine resuscitative measures as needed, since it is neither clearly normal nor clearly abnormal
Immediate emergency cesarean delivery in every case without any further assessment
No action at all, since it is equivalent to a normal (category I) tracing
Immediate termination of any further fetal monitoring
Automatic classification as category III requiring delivery within minutes
obstetrics-and-gynecology/obstetric-comp.e: A category II (indeterminate) fetal heart rate tracing requires continued surveillance and consideration of intrauterine resuscitative measures (such as maternal repositioning, oxygen, or intravenous fluids), with escalation to delivery if the pattern does not improve or progresses to category III.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/obstetric-comp.s: A woman presenting in labor with a transverse fetal lie is generally managed by which approach for delivery?
o: Routine vaginal delivery without any special precautions
Immediate application of forceps to correct the lie
Cesarean delivery, since vaginal delivery is not safely possible with a persistent transverse lie
Expectant management awaiting spontaneous correction during the second stage
Induction of labor with oxytocin regardless of the fetal lie
obstetrics-and-gynecology/obstetric-comp.e: A persistent transverse fetal lie at the onset of labor precludes safe vaginal delivery, since neither the head nor buttocks presents to the pelvis, generally necessitating cesarean delivery.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/obstetric-comp.s: Perineal lacerations sustained during vaginal delivery are classified by degree based on which anatomical extent of injury?
o: The depth of tissue involvement, ranging from superficial skin/mucosa (first degree) to involvement of the anal sphincter and rectal mucosa (third/fourth degree)
The length of the laceration in centimeters alone, regardless of depth
Whether the laceration is midline or lateral, regardless of depth
The color of the surrounding tissue
The presence or absence of bleeding, regardless of tissue involvement
obstetrics-and-gynecology/obstetric-comp.e: Perineal lacerations are classified by the depth of tissue involvement: first degree (skin/vaginal mucosa only), second degree (extending into perineal muscles), third degree (involving the anal sphincter), and fourth degree (extending through the rectal mucosa).

obstetrics-and-gynecology/obstetric-comp.s: Uterine inversion, a rare but serious complication of the third stage of labor, is characterized by which finding?
o: Complete absence of any uterine abnormality with normal fundal position
Retention of the placenta without any change in uterine position
The uterine fundus turns inside out and may protrude through the cervix or introitus
Prolapse of the umbilical cord alongside a normally positioned uterus
Rupture of the lower uterine segment with a normally oriented fundus
obstetrics-and-gynecology/obstetric-comp.e: Uterine inversion occurs when the uterine fundus turns inside out, sometimes protruding through the cervix or introitus, typically following excessive cord traction or fundal pressure during the third stage of labor, and can cause severe hemorrhage and shock requiring urgent manual replacement.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Polycystic ovary syndrome is classically diagnosed using the Rotterdam criteria, which require at least two of which three features?
o: Elevated FSH, low estrogen, and amenorrhea
Hypertension, proteinuria, and edema
Oligo/anovulation, clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism, and polycystic ovarian morphology on ultrasound
Hyperprolactinemia, galactorrhea, and amenorrhea
Elevated TSH, weight gain, and cold intolerance
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: The Rotterdam criteria diagnose polycystic ovary syndrome when at least two of three features are present: oligo-ovulation or anovulation, clinical (e.g., hirsutism, acne) or biochemical hyperandrogenism, and polycystic ovaries on ultrasound, after exclusion of other causes.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Endometriosis is defined by which pathological process?
o: Benign smooth muscle tumors within the uterine wall
Malignant transformation of endometrial glandular tissue
Abnormal thickening of the endometrium without any ectopic tissue
The presence of endometrial-like tissue outside the uterine cavity
Complete absence of the endometrial lining
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Endometriosis is characterized by the presence of functional endometrial-like glands and stroma outside the uterine cavity, most commonly on the ovaries, peritoneum, and pelvic ligaments, causing cyclical pain and potentially infertility.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Endometriosis classically presents with which combination of symptoms?
o: Painless postmenopausal bleeding
Cyclical pelvic pain, dysmenorrhea, and dyspareunia
Sudden onset of severe hypertension
Isolated galactorrhea without any pelvic pain
Chronic diarrhea without any pelvic symptoms
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Endometriosis classically presents with cyclical pelvic pain, severe dysmenorrhea, and deep dyspareunia, resulting from cyclical bleeding and inflammation of ectopic endometrial tissue, and is also a recognized cause of infertility.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: An 'endometrioma' refers to which specific finding associated with endometriosis?
o: A malignant ovarian tumor arising from endometrial tissue
A benign uterine fibroid located within the endometrial cavity
A pituitary tumor secreting excess prolactin
An ectopic pregnancy implanted within endometriotic tissue
An ovarian cyst filled with old, degenerated blood ('chocolate cyst')
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: An endometrioma, often called a 'chocolate cyst,' is an ovarian cyst formed when endometriotic tissue implants and bleeds cyclically within the ovary, producing a cyst filled with thick, dark, degenerated blood.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Uterine leiomyomas (fibroids), the most common benign tumor of the female genital tract, arise from which tissue?
o: Endometrial glandular epithelium
Uterine smooth muscle (myometrium)
Ovarian granulosa cells
Cervical squamous epithelium
Fallopian tube epithelium
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Uterine leiomyomas (fibroids) are benign monoclonal tumors arising from the smooth muscle cells of the myometrium, and are classified by location as submucosal, intramural, or subserosal.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Submucosal uterine fibroids are particularly associated with which clinical symptom, more so than other fibroid locations?
o: Urinary frequency from bladder compression as the predominant symptom
Constipation from rectal compression as the predominant symptom
Heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding and infertility
Acute abdominal pain from torsion as the predominant symptom
Galactorrhea as the predominant symptom
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Submucosal fibroids, which distort the endometrial cavity, are particularly associated with heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding (menorrhagia) and can impair implantation, contributing to infertility, more so than intramural or subserosal fibroids.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Adenomyosis, a condition in which endometrial glands and stroma are found within the myometrium, classically presents with which combination of findings?
o: A diffusely enlarged, boggy uterus with heavy menstrual bleeding and dysmenorrhea
A normal-sized uterus with painless bleeding only
An enlarged uterus with a discrete, well-circumscribed mass rather than diffuse enlargement
Complete amenorrhea without any pain
Isolated postmenopausal bleeding with a small, atrophic uterus
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Adenomyosis classically causes a diffusely enlarged, globular, and often tender ('boggy') uterus, with symptoms of heavy menstrual bleeding and progressively worsening dysmenorrhea, in contrast to the more discrete masses typical of leiomyomas.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Abnormal uterine bleeding in a woman over 45 years of age requires which key investigation to exclude endometrial malignancy?
o: Serum CA-125 measurement as the definitive diagnostic test
Chest X-ray as the definitive diagnostic test
Endometrial biopsy or sampling
Colposcopy as the definitive diagnostic test for endometrial pathology
Mammography as the definitive diagnostic test for endometrial pathology
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Abnormal uterine bleeding in women over 45 (or with risk factors at any age) warrants endometrial sampling (biopsy) to exclude endometrial hyperplasia or carcinoma, given the increasing risk of malignancy with age and unopposed estrogen exposure.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Endometrial hyperplasia, a precursor lesion for endometrial carcinoma in some cases, results from which underlying hormonal imbalance?
o: Excess progesterone relative to estrogen
Complete absence of both estrogen and progesterone
Unopposed estrogen stimulation of the endometrium without adequate progesterone counterbalance
Excess thyroid hormone acting directly on the endometrium
Excess growth hormone acting directly on the endometrium
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Endometrial hyperplasia typically results from chronic unopposed estrogen stimulation of the endometrium (as seen in anovulatory cycles, obesity, or estrogen-only hormone therapy) without adequate progesterone to induce secretory differentiation and shedding.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Primary dysmenorrhea, painful menstruation without an identifiable pelvic pathology, is primarily attributed to which mechanism?
o: A structural uterine anomaly present from birth
Chronic pelvic infection in the majority of cases
Advanced endometrial cancer in young women
A vitamin deficiency as the primary underlying cause
Excess endometrial prostaglandin production causing uterine hypercontractility and ischemia
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Primary dysmenorrhea results from excess endometrial prostaglandin (particularly PGF2-alpha) production during menstruation, causing excessive uterine muscle contraction, reduced blood flow, and resultant ischemic pain, typically responsive to NSAIDs which inhibit prostaglandin synthesis.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Secondary dysmenorrhea, unlike primary dysmenorrhea, is characterized by which feature?
o: Onset exclusively before the first menstrual period
Complete absence of any pelvic pain
An identifiable underlying pelvic pathology, such as endometriosis or fibroids
Occurrence exclusively in postmenopausal women
A normal pelvic examination and imaging in all cases, by definition
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Secondary dysmenorrhea is menstrual pain attributable to an identifiable underlying pelvic pathology, such as endometriosis, adenomyosis, or fibroids, distinguishing it from primary dysmenorrhea, which occurs without such structural pathology.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Asherman syndrome, a cause of secondary amenorrhea and infertility, results from which pathological process?
o: Ovarian failure due to autoimmune destruction
A pituitary adenoma secreting excess prolactin
Congenital absence of the uterus
Intrauterine adhesions (synechiae), often following uterine curettage or infection
Excess estrogen production from an ovarian tumor
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Asherman syndrome results from intrauterine adhesions (synechiae) forming after endometrial trauma, most commonly following dilation and curettage (especially postpartum or post-abortion) or endometrial infection, leading to amenorrhea and infertility from a scarred, non-functional endometrial cavity.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: A functional ovarian cyst, such as a follicular or corpus luteum cyst, is generally managed in an asymptomatic premenopausal woman by which approach?
o: Immediate surgical removal in all cases regardless of size or symptoms
Immediate chemotherapy
Observation with follow-up ultrasound, as most resolve spontaneously
Hormone replacement therapy as the definitive treatment
Radiotherapy directed at the ovary
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Functional ovarian cysts (follicular or corpus luteum cysts) are common, benign, and typically resolve spontaneously within one to a few menstrual cycles, so observation with interval ultrasound is generally appropriate in asymptomatic premenopausal women, reserving intervention for persistent, enlarging, or symptomatic cysts.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Ovarian torsion, a gynecological emergency, classically presents with which clinical picture?
o: Gradual onset of bilateral pelvic pain over several weeks
Painless pelvic mass discovered incidentally with no associated symptoms
Chronic, mild pelvic discomfort without any acute component
Isolated vaginal bleeding without any pain
Sudden onset of severe unilateral pelvic pain, often with nausea and vomiting
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Ovarian torsion classically presents with sudden onset of severe, often unilateral pelvic pain, frequently accompanied by nausea and vomiting, resulting from twisting of the ovary (and often the fallopian tube) on its vascular pedicle, compromising blood supply and constituting a surgical emergency.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: A dermoid cyst (mature cystic teratoma) of the ovary, a common benign ovarian tumor particularly in young women, is characterized by which histological feature?
o: Exclusively glandular epithelial tissue resembling the endometrium
Pure smooth muscle tissue identical to a uterine fibroid
Exclusively neural tissue derived from ectoderm alone
Exclusively fatty tissue with no other tissue types present
Tissue derived from all three germ cell layers, including hair, teeth, and sebaceous material
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: A mature cystic teratoma (dermoid cyst) contains well-differentiated tissue derived from all three germ cell layers (ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm), commonly including hair, sebaceous material, teeth, and sometimes other tissue types, reflecting its origin from a totipotent germ cell.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Premature ovarian insufficiency refers to which clinical condition?
o: Delayed onset of menarche beyond the age of 16 years
Normal age-appropriate menopause occurring around age 50-52
Loss of normal ovarian function before the age of 40 years
A benign ovarian cyst discovered before age 40
Excess ovarian hormone production before age 40
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Premature ovarian insufficiency is defined as the loss of normal ovarian function (with amenorrhea and elevated gonadotropins) before the age of 40 years, resulting in estrogen deficiency and infertility, from various causes including genetic, autoimmune, or iatrogenic factors.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Pelvic inflammatory disease, an infection of the upper female genital tract, is most commonly caused by which group of organisms?
o: Mycobacterium tuberculosis as the most common cause worldwide
Candida albicans as the most common causative organism
Sexually transmitted organisms such as Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae
Human papillomavirus as the most common causative organism
Herpes simplex virus as the most common causative organism
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Pelvic inflammatory disease is most commonly caused by ascending infection with sexually transmitted organisms, particularly Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae, though it is often polymicrobial, involving additional endogenous vaginal flora.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: A tubo-ovarian abscess, a serious complication of pelvic inflammatory disease, is best initially evaluated using which imaging modality?
o: Plain abdominal X-ray as the initial imaging study
Barium enema as the initial imaging study
Pelvic ultrasound
Chest CT scan as the initial imaging study
Mammography as the initial imaging study
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Pelvic ultrasound is the initial imaging modality of choice for suspected tubo-ovarian abscess, allowing identification of a complex adnexal mass and guiding decisions regarding antibiotic therapy versus surgical or radiological drainage.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Chronic, untreated pelvic inflammatory disease significantly increases the long-term risk of which reproductive complication?
o: Tubal factor infertility and ectopic pregnancy from tubal scarring
Uterine fibroids as the primary long-term complication
Endometrial cancer as the primary long-term complication
Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome as the primary long-term complication
Premature ovarian insufficiency as the primary long-term complication
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Chronic or recurrent pelvic inflammatory disease causes fallopian tube scarring and adhesions, significantly increasing the long-term risk of tubal factor infertility and ectopic pregnancy due to impaired tubal transport of the fertilized ovum.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Bacterial vaginosis, a common cause of abnormal vaginal discharge, is characterized by which laboratory/clinical finding?
o: A shift in vaginal flora with a fishy odor, thin grayish-white discharge, and clue cells on microscopy
Intense vulvar itching with thick, curd-like white discharge
Frothy, yellow-green discharge with a strawberry cervix
Purulent cervical discharge with cervical motion tenderness as the primary finding
Complete absence of any vaginal discharge
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Bacterial vaginosis results from a shift in vaginal flora (reduced lactobacilli, overgrowth of anaerobes such as Gardnerella vaginalis) causing a characteristic fishy-odored, thin, grayish-white discharge, with clue cells (epithelial cells coated with bacteria) seen on microscopy.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Vulvovaginal candidiasis classically presents with which type of vaginal discharge and associated symptom?
o: Thin, grayish-white discharge with a fishy odor and minimal itching
Frothy, greenish-yellow discharge with a strawberry cervix
Watery, blood-tinged discharge with no itching
Purulent, foul-smelling discharge with fever
Thick, white, curd-like ('cottage cheese') discharge with intense vulvar itching
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Vulvovaginal candidiasis classically presents with a thick, white, curd-like ('cottage cheese') vaginal discharge accompanied by intense vulvar and vaginal itching and erythema, often exacerbated by factors such as antibiotic use, diabetes, or pregnancy.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Trichomonas vaginalis infection classically causes which type of vaginal discharge, along with cervical findings on examination?
o: Thick, white, curd-like discharge with intense itching
Thin, grayish discharge with a fishy odor and clue cells
Frothy, yellow-green, malodorous discharge with a 'strawberry cervix' appearance
A completely asymptomatic presentation in all infected women
Bloody discharge with cervical friability as the classic finding
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Trichomonas vaginalis, a sexually transmitted protozoan infection, classically causes a frothy, yellow-green, malodorous vaginal discharge, sometimes accompanied by a punctate 'strawberry cervix' appearance from cervical capillary inflammation.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Lichen sclerosus, a chronic inflammatory skin condition affecting the vulva, is clinically significant because of its association with which long-term risk?
o: Direct progression to cervical cancer in the majority of cases
An increased risk of ovarian cancer
Complete resolution without any long-term risk in all patients
An increased risk of vulvar squamous cell carcinoma
An increased risk of endometrial cancer as the primary long-term concern
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Lichen sclerosus causes chronic vulvar itching, pain, and characteristic thin, white, 'cigarette paper' skin changes, and carries a modestly increased long-term risk of vulvar squamous cell carcinoma, warranting long-term monitoring.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Amenorrhea occurring in a woman who has never menstruated by age 15 (or within 5 years of thelarche) is classified as which type?
o: Secondary amenorrhea
Primary amenorrhea
Physiological amenorrhea of pregnancy
Postmenopausal amenorrhea
Lactational amenorrhea
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Primary amenorrhea refers to the absence of menarche by age 15 (in the presence of normal growth and secondary sexual characteristics) or within 5 years of thelarche (breast development), warranting evaluation for underlying anatomical, genetic, or endocrine causes.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Secondary amenorrhea is defined as the absence of menstruation for how long in a woman who has previously had normal menstrual cycles?
o: One missed cycle only, regardless of prior regularity
24 hours without menstrual bleeding
One full year without exception, regardless of prior cycle regularity
Three or more consecutive months (or six months in women with prior irregular cycles)
Ten years without exception
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Secondary amenorrhea is generally defined as the absence of menstruation for three or more consecutive months in a woman with previously regular cycles (or six months in a woman with previously irregular cycles), most commonly due to pregnancy but requiring evaluation of other causes when pregnancy is excluded.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Hyperprolactinemia, a recognized cause of secondary amenorrhea, most commonly results from which underlying cause?
o: Primary ovarian failure as the most common cause of hyperprolactinemia
Excess androgen production from the adrenal gland as the most common cause
Hyperthyroidism as the most common cause of hyperprolactinemia
Uterine fibroids as the most common cause of hyperprolactinemia
A prolactin-secreting pituitary adenoma (prolactinoma)
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: A prolactin-secreting pituitary adenoma (prolactinoma) is the most common pathological cause of hyperprolactinemia, which suppresses gonadotropin-releasing hormone pulsatility, leading to amenorrhea and often galactorrhea.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: A urinary or vaginal fistula (e.g., vesicovaginal fistula) in resource-limited settings is most commonly caused by which obstetric complication?
o: Elective cesarean section performed without complication
Normal spontaneous vaginal delivery without any complication
Prolonged, obstructed labor causing pressure necrosis of adjacent tissues
Postpartum hemorrhage alone, without any prolonged labor
Routine episiotomy performed without complication
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: In many resource-limited settings, obstetric vesicovaginal fistula most commonly results from prolonged, obstructed labor, where sustained pressure of the fetal head against the maternal pelvis causes ischemic necrosis of the bladder and vaginal walls, creating an abnormal communication.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Uterine prolapse, the descent of the uterus into or through the vaginal canal, is most strongly associated with which risk factor?
o: Multiparity and vaginal delivery, causing weakening of pelvic floor support structures
Nulliparity as the primary and most significant risk factor
Young age at first pregnancy as the primary risk factor
Cesarean delivery as the primary risk factor, more so than vaginal delivery
Male sex, as it also occurs commonly in men
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Uterine prolapse is most strongly associated with multiparity and vaginal delivery (particularly with prolonged second stages or instrumental delivery), which weaken the pelvic floor musculature and connective tissue support of the uterus over time; other risk factors include aging, obesity, and chronic increased intra-abdominal pressure.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Hirsutism in a woman with polycystic ovary syndrome results from which underlying hormonal abnormality?
o: Elevated estrogen levels acting directly on hair follicles
Elevated prolactin levels acting directly on hair follicles
Elevated circulating androgen levels acting on androgen-sensitive hair follicles
Reduced thyroid hormone levels acting on hair follicles
Elevated progesterone levels acting on hair follicles
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Hirsutism in polycystic ovary syndrome results from elevated circulating androgen levels (from ovarian and sometimes adrenal sources) acting on androgen-sensitive hair follicles, causing excess terminal hair growth in a male-pattern distribution.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Women with polycystic ovary syndrome are at increased long-term risk for which metabolic complication?
o: Hyperthyroidism as the primary long-term metabolic risk
Insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes mellitus
Adrenal insufficiency as the primary long-term metabolic risk
Hypocalcemia as the primary long-term metabolic risk
Vitamin B12 deficiency as the primary long-term metabolic risk
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Polycystic ovary syndrome is strongly associated with insulin resistance, significantly increasing the long-term risk of impaired glucose tolerance and type 2 diabetes mellitus, in addition to its reproductive manifestations.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Laparoscopy remains an important diagnostic and therapeutic tool for which gynecological condition, allowing direct visualization and excision or ablation of lesions?
o: Uncomplicated bacterial vaginosis
Endometriosis
Uncomplicated vulvovaginal candidiasis
Primary dysmenorrhea without any suspected pathology
Simple, asymptomatic functional ovarian cysts
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Laparoscopy allows direct visualization of pelvic structures and is considered the gold standard for definitive diagnosis of endometriosis, with the added benefit of allowing simultaneous surgical excision or ablation of endometriotic implants.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: GnRH agonists are sometimes used in the medical management of endometriosis and fibroids primarily through which mechanism?
o: Directly increasing estrogen production to shrink lesions
Inducing a hypoestrogenic state by initially stimulating then desensitizing pituitary gonadotropin release
Direct surgical destruction of ectopic endometrial tissue
Stimulating ovulation to relieve symptoms
Increasing androgen levels to suppress the endometrium
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: GnRH agonists initially stimulate, then (with continuous administration) desensitize pituitary GnRH receptors, suppressing gonadotropin and consequently ovarian estrogen production, inducing a temporary hypoestrogenic, pseudo-menopausal state that can reduce endometriosis symptoms and fibroid size.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Uterine artery embolization is a treatment option for symptomatic fibroids that works by which mechanism?
o: Directly incising and removing the fibroid through the abdominal wall
Occluding the blood supply to the fibroid, causing it to shrink through ischemic infarction
Increasing blood flow to the fibroid to promote reabsorption
Ablating the endometrial lining directly, without addressing the fibroid's blood supply
Inducing ovulation to naturally shrink the fibroid
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Uterine artery embolization involves selective catheterization and occlusion of the uterine arteries supplying the fibroid, inducing ischemic infarction and subsequent shrinkage of the fibroid while generally preserving the uterus.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: A hysteroscopy allows direct visualization and, when needed, treatment of which structure?
o: The endometrial cavity
The ovarian surface exclusively
The peritoneal cavity exclusively
The fallopian tube lumen in its entirety, from fimbria to cornua
The external cervix and vulva exclusively
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Hysteroscopy involves passage of a thin, lighted instrument through the cervix to directly visualize and, when indicated, treat pathology within the endometrial cavity, such as submucosal fibroids, polyps, or intrauterine adhesions.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: An endometrial polyp, a common benign gynecological finding, most frequently presents with which symptom?
o: Chronic pelvic pain as the most common presenting symptom
Galactorrhea as the most common presenting symptom
Abnormal or intermenstrual uterine bleeding
Acute abdominal pain from torsion, as the most common presentation
Hirsutism as the most common presenting symptom
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Endometrial polyps, localized overgrowths of endometrial tissue, most commonly present with abnormal uterine bleeding, including intermenstrual bleeding or postmenopausal bleeding, and are often diagnosed by transvaginal ultrasound or hysteroscopy.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Premenstrual syndrome refers to which cluster of symptoms?
o: Symptoms that occur exclusively during pregnancy
Recurrent physical and emotional symptoms occurring in the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle that resolve with menstruation
Symptoms that occur exclusively after menopause
A permanent, non-cyclical mood disorder unrelated to the menstrual cycle
Symptoms occurring exclusively during the follicular phase of the cycle
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Premenstrual syndrome consists of a cluster of physical (e.g., bloating, breast tenderness) and emotional (e.g., irritability, mood lability) symptoms that recur predictably during the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle and resolve with the onset of menstruation.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Pelvic organ prolapse is commonly assessed and staged using which clinical tool?
o: The Bishop score
The Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification (POP-Q) system
The Apgar score
The Rotterdam criteria
The Gleason grading system
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: The Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification (POP-Q) system is a standardized clinical tool used to objectively assess and stage the severity and location of pelvic organ prolapse, based on measurements relative to the hymen.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Stress urinary incontinence, characterized by involuntary urine leakage with increased intra-abdominal pressure (e.g., coughing, sneezing), results primarily from which underlying mechanism?
o: Overactivity (involuntary contraction) of the detrusor muscle
A urinary tract infection in the majority of cases
A neurological lesion affecting bladder innervation in the majority of cases
Weakness of the pelvic floor musculature and urethral sphincter support
Complete bladder outlet obstruction
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Stress urinary incontinence results from weakness of pelvic floor support structures and the urethral sphincter mechanism, allowing urine leakage when intra-abdominal pressure increases (e.g., with coughing or exertion), overcoming the compromised urethral closure pressure.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Urge urinary incontinence, associated with a sudden compelling desire to void that is difficult to defer, results primarily from which mechanism?
o: Pure anatomical weakness of the pelvic floor without any bladder overactivity
A fixed, mechanical bladder outlet obstruction
A vesicovaginal fistula
Chronic vulvar dermatosis
Involuntary detrusor muscle contractions (overactive bladder)
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Urge urinary incontinence results from involuntary detrusor muscle contractions during bladder filling (overactive bladder), causing a sudden, strong urge to void and often leakage before reaching a toilet, distinguishing it from the purely mechanical mechanism of stress incontinence.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: A rectovaginal examination is particularly useful in gynecological assessment for evaluating which structure or condition?
o: The anterior abdominal wall exclusively
The thyroid gland exclusively
The breast tissue exclusively
The axillary lymph nodes exclusively
The posterior pelvis, including uterosacral ligaments and rectovaginal septum, useful in assessing suspected endometriosis or posterior pelvic masses
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: A rectovaginal examination allows palpation of the posterior pelvic structures, including the uterosacral ligaments and rectovaginal septum, which is particularly useful for detecting nodularity or tenderness suggestive of endometriosis or assessing posterior pelvic masses not well felt on vaginal examination alone.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Persistent infection with high-risk types of which virus is the necessary underlying cause of the vast majority of cervical cancer cases?
o: Herpes simplex virus
Epstein-Barr virus
Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) directly
Human papillomavirus (HPV)
Cytomegalovirus
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus types (particularly HPV 16 and 18) is the necessary causal factor in the vast majority of cervical cancer cases, driving progression through precancerous dysplastic changes to invasive carcinoma.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Cervical cancer screening using cytology (Pap smear) is designed primarily to detect which stage of disease?
o: Metastatic disease that has already spread beyond the pelvis
End-stage cervical cancer only
Precancerous cervical intraepithelial lesions before progression to invasive cancer
Only cervical infections unrelated to any precancerous change
Only ovarian cancer, since cervical screening also covers ovarian pathology
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Cervical cytology screening is designed to detect precancerous cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (dysplasia) at an early, treatable stage, before progression to invasive cervical carcinoma, allowing for timely intervention.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: The HPV vaccine is most effective when administered at which point relative to sexual debut?
o: Only after a woman has already been diagnosed with cervical cancer
Only during pregnancy
Before the onset of sexual activity, typically in early adolescence
Only after menopause
Only in men, since it provides no benefit to women
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: The HPV vaccine provides the greatest benefit when administered before the onset of sexual activity (and therefore before likely HPV exposure), typically recommended in early adolescence, though catch-up vaccination is also offered to older individuals.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: The most common presenting symptom of cervical cancer is which of the following?
o: Abnormal vaginal bleeding, particularly postcoital bleeding
Painless abdominal distension as the most common presenting symptom
Chronic constipation as the most common presenting symptom
Galactorrhea as the most common presenting symptom
Bilateral leg swelling as the most common presenting symptom
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Abnormal vaginal bleeding, particularly postcoital bleeding, is the most common presenting symptom of cervical cancer, though early-stage disease (including precancerous lesions detected by screening) may be entirely asymptomatic.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Endometrial carcinoma, the most common gynecological malignancy in many high-income countries, is most strongly associated with which risk factor?
o: Unopposed estrogen exposure (e.g., obesity, anovulation, estrogen-only hormone therapy)
Multiparity as the predominant risk factor
Early menopause as the predominant risk factor
Smoking as the predominant risk factor for endometrial cancer
Low body mass index as the predominant risk factor
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Endometrial carcinoma (endometrioid type) is most strongly associated with conditions causing unopposed estrogen exposure, including obesity (peripheral aromatization of androgens to estrogen), chronic anovulation (as in polycystic ovary syndrome), nulliparity, and unopposed estrogen hormone therapy.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: The most common presenting symptom of endometrial carcinoma, often prompting early diagnosis, is which of the following?
o: Painless abdominal mass as the most common presenting symptom
Chronic pelvic pain as the most common presenting symptom
Galactorrhea as the most common presenting symptom
Postmenopausal bleeding
Bilateral leg edema as the most common presenting symptom
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Postmenopausal bleeding is the most common and important presenting symptom of endometrial carcinoma, and any postmenopausal bleeding warrants prompt investigation (typically with endometrial biopsy and/or transvaginal ultrasound) to exclude malignancy.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Ovarian cancer often presents at an advanced stage because of which characteristic feature of the disease?
o: It is universally asymptomatic even at advanced stages
It causes early, severe pain that is often misdiagnosed as a benign condition
Early symptoms are typically vague and nonspecific (e.g., bloating, early satiety), delaying diagnosis
There is an effective, widely used screening test that is simply underutilized
It exclusively affects women after the disease has already metastasized to the brain
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Ovarian cancer often presents at an advanced stage because early symptoms (bloating, early satiety, vague abdominal or pelvic discomfort, urinary frequency) are nonspecific and easily attributed to other, more common conditions, and no effective population-based screening test currently exists.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Which tumor marker is commonly used to monitor treatment response and detect recurrence in epithelial ovarian cancer, though it lacks sufficient specificity for population screening?
o: Alpha-fetoprotein as the primary marker for epithelial ovarian cancer
Human chorionic gonadotropin as the primary marker for epithelial ovarian cancer
Prostate-specific antigen
Carcinoembryonic antigen as the primary marker for epithelial ovarian cancer
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: CA-125 is the most widely used tumor marker for epithelial ovarian cancer, useful for monitoring treatment response and detecting recurrence, though its elevation in various benign conditions limits its usefulness as a standalone population screening test.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Vulvar cancer, most commonly squamous cell carcinoma, is associated with which two distinct etiological pathways?
o: Exclusively HPV infection regardless of patient age
HPV-related disease in younger women and lichen sclerosus/chronic vulvar dermatosis-related disease in older women
Exclusively hormonal factors unrelated to HPV or dermatosis
Exclusively hereditary genetic mutations with no environmental contribution
Exclusively related to prior chemotherapy exposure
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Vulvar squamous cell carcinoma arises through two main pathways: an HPV-related pathway more common in younger women (associated with vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia), and a pathway related to chronic vulvar dermatoses such as lichen sclerosus, more common in older women.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Gestational trophoblastic disease, including hydatidiform mole, arises from abnormal proliferation of which tissue?
o: Normal endometrial glandular tissue
Ovarian germ cell tissue
Cervical squamous epithelium
Trophoblastic tissue derived from an abnormally fertilized ovum
Fallopian tube smooth muscle
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Gestational trophoblastic disease encompasses a spectrum of conditions arising from abnormal proliferation of trophoblastic tissue following an abnormal fertilization event, ranging from benign hydatidiform mole to malignant choriocarcinoma.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: A complete hydatidiform mole classically arises from which genetic mechanism?
o: Fertilization of a normal ovum by two separate sperm, yielding a normal diploid genome with a fetus present
A spontaneous chromosomal deletion in an otherwise normal pregnancy with a viable fetus
A maternal-only (parthenogenetic) origin with no paternal contribution
Fertilization of an empty ovum (lacking maternal genetic material) by one sperm that duplicates, or by two sperm, yielding a diploid, entirely paternal genome
Triploidy from fertilization of a normal ovum by two sperm, with a coexisting abnormal fetus
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: A complete hydatidiform mole typically results from fertilization of an ovum that has lost its maternal genetic material by a single sperm that then duplicates its own genome (or by two sperm), yielding a diploid genome that is entirely paternal in origin, with no fetal tissue present.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: A hydatidiform mole classically presents with which combination of clinical and laboratory findings?
o: Vaginal bleeding with a uterus larger than expected for gestational age and markedly elevated beta-hCG levels
Painless bleeding with a uterus smaller than expected and low beta-hCG levels
Complete absence of any vaginal bleeding with normal beta-hCG levels
Isolated hypertension without any bleeding or uterine size abnormality
A normal ultrasound with a clearly visible, viable fetus
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: A hydatidiform mole classically presents with vaginal bleeding, a uterus that is often larger than expected for gestational age (from trophoblastic proliferation), and markedly elevated serum beta-hCG levels, with a characteristic 'snowstorm' appearance on ultrasound and absence of a normal fetus in complete moles.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: After evacuation of a hydatidiform mole, which follow-up protocol is essential to detect the development of persistent or malignant gestational trophoblastic disease?
o: Serial serum beta-hCG monitoring until it returns to and remains at undetectable levels
A single beta-hCG measurement immediately after evacuation, with no further follow-up needed
Annual mammography as the primary follow-up test
Routine chest X-ray alone, without any beta-hCG monitoring
No follow-up is required after successful evacuation
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Following molar evacuation, serial serum beta-hCG levels are monitored until they return to and remain at undetectable levels, since a plateau or rise indicates persistent or malignant gestational trophoblastic disease (invasive mole or choriocarcinoma) requiring further treatment, often with chemotherapy.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: An ectopic pregnancy, in which implantation occurs outside the uterine cavity, occurs most commonly at which anatomical site?
o: The ovary as the most common site
The cervix as the most common site
The abdominal cavity as the most common site
The broad ligament as the most common site
The fallopian tube (particularly the ampullary portion)
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: The fallopian tube, particularly its ampullary segment, is by far the most common site of ectopic implantation, though ectopic pregnancies can rarely occur in the ovary, cervix, abdominal cavity, or at a prior cesarean scar.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: A ruptured ectopic pregnancy is a gynecological emergency that classically presents with which combination of features?
o: Gradual onset of bilateral lower limb swelling without any abdominal pain
Painless, heavy vaginal bleeding with a stable hemodynamic status
Isolated fever without any abdominal pain or bleeding
Chronic, mild pelvic discomfort persisting over several months
Sudden severe unilateral abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, and signs of hemodynamic instability
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: A ruptured ectopic pregnancy classically presents with sudden severe unilateral abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, and signs of hemodynamic instability (tachycardia, hypotension) from intra-abdominal hemorrhage, constituting a surgical emergency.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Methotrexate is used for the medical management of an unruptured ectopic pregnancy primarily by which mechanism of action?
o: Directly inducing uterine contractions to expel the pregnancy
Blocking progesterone receptors to terminate the pregnancy
Directly lysing red blood cells within the ectopic gestational sac
Inhibiting dihydrofolate reductase, thereby disrupting rapidly dividing trophoblastic cells
Stimulating maternal immune rejection of the ectopic tissue
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Methotrexate, a folate antagonist that inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, disrupts DNA synthesis in rapidly dividing trophoblastic cells, making it effective for medical management of an appropriately selected, hemodynamically stable, unruptured ectopic pregnancy.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Toxic shock syndrome, historically associated with prolonged tampon use, is caused by toxins produced by which organism?
o: Neisseria gonorrhoeae as the classic causative organism
Staphylococcus aureus
Chlamydia trachomatis as the classic causative organism
Trichomonas vaginalis as the classic causative organism
Candida albicans as the classic causative organism
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Toxic shock syndrome is caused by toxin-producing strains of Staphylococcus aureus (particularly toxic shock syndrome toxin-1), classically associated with prolonged high-absorbency tampon use, though it can also occur in other contexts involving Staphylococcal infection.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Genital herpes, caused by herpes simplex virus, is characterized by which classic clinical presentation?
o: Painful, grouped vesicles on an erythematous base that progress to shallow ulcers
Painless, indurated ulcers (chancres) as the classic presentation
A single, painless, wart-like lesion as the classic presentation
Widespread, non-itchy, coppery-colored rash on the palms and soles
Frothy vaginal discharge without any skin lesions
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Genital herpes classically presents with painful, grouped vesicles on an erythematous base that rupture to form shallow, painful ulcers, often accompanied by local lymphadenopathy and, in primary infection, systemic symptoms.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Primary syphilis, caused by Treponema pallidum, classically presents with which genital lesion?
o: A painful, tender ulcer with a purulent base
Multiple painful vesicular lesions
A wart-like, cauliflower-shaped growth
A diffuse maculopapular rash without any ulceration
A painless, indurated ulcer (chancre) at the site of inoculation
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Primary syphilis classically presents with a single, painless, indurated ulcer (chancre) with a clean base at the site of Treponema pallidum inoculation, often accompanied by regional lymphadenopathy, and typically resolves spontaneously even without treatment before progressing to secondary syphilis if untreated.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Genital warts (condylomata acuminata) are caused by which HPV subtypes, distinct from the high-risk oncogenic types?
o: HPV types 16 and 18, the same types associated with cervical cancer
HPV types 31 and 33 exclusively
HPV types 45 and 52 exclusively
All HPV types cause genital warts equally, with no distinction between subtypes
HPV types 6 and 11
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Genital warts (condylomata acuminata) are most commonly caused by low-risk HPV types 6 and 11, which have low oncogenic potential, in contrast to the high-risk types (16 and 18, among others) most strongly associated with cervical and other anogenital cancers.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Chlamydia trachomatis genital infection in women is clinically significant in part because it is frequently which type of infection?
o: Always symptomatic with severe pain, making diagnosis straightforward in all cases
Exclusively transmitted through non-sexual contact
Curable only with prolonged multi-year antibiotic courses
Asymptomatic, allowing silent progression to pelvic inflammatory disease and tubal damage if untreated
Associated exclusively with oral, not genital, manifestations
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Chlamydia trachomatis infection in women is frequently asymptomatic, which allows silent ascending infection and progression to pelvic inflammatory disease, tubal scarring, and subsequent infertility or ectopic pregnancy risk if left undiagnosed and untreated, underscoring the importance of screening in sexually active young women.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), a precursor to cervical cancer, is graded (CIN 1, 2, 3) based on which histological feature?
o: The size of the lesion in centimeters as measured on colposcopy
The patient's age at diagnosis
The proportion of the epithelial thickness occupied by abnormal, dysplastic cells
The presence or absence of vaginal bleeding
The patient's HPV vaccination status
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia is graded based on the proportion of the epithelial thickness replaced by dysplastic cells: CIN 1 involves the lower third, CIN 2 the lower two-thirds, and CIN 3 involves greater than two-thirds or the full thickness of the epithelium.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: A colposcopy-directed cervical biopsy is generally indicated following which finding?
o: A completely normal Pap smear result
An abnormal cervical cytology (Pap smear) result requiring further evaluation of the transformation zone
A normal pelvic ultrasound with no cervical abnormality noted
Routine screening in all women regardless of cytology results
A negative HPV test in a woman with normal cytology
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Colposcopy, with directed biopsy of visually abnormal areas, is indicated following an abnormal cervical cytology result (or persistent high-risk HPV positivity) to further evaluate and histologically confirm the presence and grade of any cervical dysplasia.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: The FIGO staging system, used for cervical, endometrial, and ovarian cancers, primarily incorporates which factor to define stage?
o: The patient's age at diagnosis exclusively
The tumor marker level exclusively, independent of anatomical findings
The patient's parity exclusively
The anatomical extent of tumor spread, including local invasion, lymph node involvement, and distant metastasis
The histological subtype exclusively, independent of anatomical extent
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: The FIGO staging system for gynecological cancers is based primarily on the anatomical extent of disease, including the size and local extent of the primary tumor, regional lymph node involvement, and the presence or absence of distant metastasis.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Radical hysterectomy with pelvic lymphadenectomy is a standard surgical treatment option for which stage of cervical cancer?
o: Advanced metastatic cervical cancer with distant spread to the lungs or liver
Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 1 (CIN 1) only
Only in cases of recurrent disease after prior radiotherapy
Only when the patient is postmenopausal, regardless of stage
Early-stage, operable cervical cancer confined to the cervix or with limited local extension
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Radical hysterectomy with pelvic lymphadenectomy is a standard treatment option for early-stage, operable cervical cancer, while more advanced disease is generally managed with chemoradiation rather than primary surgery.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Serous carcinoma is a histological subtype of endometrial cancer associated with which prognostic characteristic compared to the more common endometrioid subtype?
o: An identical prognosis to endometrioid carcinoma in all respects
A more aggressive clinical course and generally worse prognosis, often unrelated to unopposed estrogen exposure
A universally excellent prognosis regardless of stage
Exclusive occurrence in premenopausal women
A strong association specifically with unopposed estrogen exposure, more so than endometrioid carcinoma
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Serous carcinoma of the endometrium (a type II endometrial cancer) tends to behave more aggressively and carries a worse prognosis than the more common endometrioid (type I) carcinoma, and is less consistently associated with unopposed estrogen exposure.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Epithelial tumors are the most common histological category of ovarian neoplasm; which other broad category, though less common, includes tumors such as dysgerminoma?
o: Vascular tumors as the category including dysgerminoma
Germ cell tumors
Purely fibrous stromal tumors as the category including dysgerminoma
Metastatic tumors from a primary colonic source exclusively
Squamous cell tumors arising from ovarian surface epithelium
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Germ cell tumors, including dysgerminoma (the ovarian counterpart of testicular seminoma), are a distinct category of ovarian neoplasm arising from primordial germ cells, occurring more commonly in younger women compared to the more common epithelial ovarian tumors.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: A granulosa cell tumor of the ovary, a sex cord-stromal tumor, is clinically notable for which hormonal effect?
o: Androgen secretion causing virilization in the majority of cases
No hormonal activity in the vast majority of cases
Excess cortisol secretion causing Cushingoid features
Estrogen secretion, which can cause precocious puberty in girls or postmenopausal bleeding in older women
Excess parathyroid hormone-related peptide secretion causing hypercalcemia
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Granulosa cell tumors are estrogen-secreting sex cord-stromal tumors of the ovary, which can cause precocious puberty if occurring in prepubertal girls or abnormal (often postmenopausal) uterine bleeding and endometrial hyperplasia in older women due to unopposed estrogen stimulation.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutation carriers are at significantly increased risk for which gynecological malignancy, in addition to breast cancer?
o: Epithelial ovarian (and fallopian tube) cancer
Vulvar squamous cell carcinoma as the primary additional gynecological risk
Gestational trophoblastic disease as the primary additional gynecological risk
Cervical squamous cell carcinoma as the primary additional gynecological risk specifically related to BRCA mutations
Vaginal clear cell adenocarcinoma as the primary additional gynecological risk
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutation carriers have a significantly increased lifetime risk of epithelial ovarian cancer (including tumors now understood to often originate in the fallopian tube), in addition to their markedly increased breast cancer risk, prompting consideration of risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Diethylstilbestrol exposure in utero, historically prescribed to pregnant women, is associated with an increased risk of which rare malignancy in exposed daughters?
o: Choriocarcinoma as the primary associated malignancy
Endometrial serous carcinoma as the primary associated malignancy
Vulvar squamous cell carcinoma as the primary associated malignancy
Ovarian germ cell tumors as the primary associated malignancy
Clear cell adenocarcinoma of the vagina or cervix
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: In utero exposure to diethylstilbestrol, a synthetic estrogen once used to prevent miscarriage, is associated with an increased risk of clear cell adenocarcinoma of the vagina or cervix in exposed daughters, along with structural reproductive tract anomalies.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection in women, if untreated, can ascend to cause pelvic inflammatory disease, but may also cause disseminated infection presenting with which finding?
o: A triad of dermatitis, tenosynovitis, and migratory polyarthralgia/arthritis
Isolated hepatosplenomegaly without any joint or skin involvement
Isolated cardiac valvular vegetations without any skin or joint findings
Progressive dementia as the primary manifestation of disseminated infection
Isolated renal failure as the primary manifestation of disseminated infection
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Disseminated gonococcal infection classically presents with a triad of dermatitis (pustular or vesiculopustular skin lesions), tenosynovitis, and migratory polyarthralgia or septic arthritis, resulting from hematogenous spread of Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Congenital syphilis, resulting from transplacental transmission of Treponema pallidum, can be prevented primarily through which measure?
o: Cesarean delivery in all syphilis-positive pregnancies, regardless of treatment status
Avoidance of breastfeeding in syphilis-positive mothers
Administration of the HPV vaccine during pregnancy
Avoidance of vaginal delivery in all pregnancies regardless of syphilis status
Universal antenatal syphilis screening and prompt maternal treatment with penicillin
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Congenital syphilis is effectively prevented through universal antenatal screening for syphilis and prompt, adequate maternal treatment with penicillin, which crosses the placenta and treats the fetus as well when given early enough in pregnancy.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: A Bartholin gland cyst or abscess arises from obstruction of which structure?
o: The duct of the Bartholin gland, located at the posterior introitus
The urethral (Skene's) glands
The cervical os
The fallopian tube ostium
The ureteric orifice within the bladder
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: A Bartholin gland cyst or abscess results from obstruction of the duct of the Bartholin gland (located at the posterolateral vaginal introitus), causing accumulation of gland secretions and, if infected, abscess formation, typically managed with incision and drainage or marsupialization.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection increases a woman's risk of more rapid progression and recurrence of which HPV-related gynecological condition?
o: Uncomplicated bacterial vaginosis as the primary HPV-related condition affected
Simple functional ovarian cysts as the primary condition affected
Primary dysmenorrhea as the primary condition affected
Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and invasive cervical cancer
Uterine fibroids as the primary condition affected
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: HIV infection, through its effects on cell-mediated immunity, is associated with more rapid progression and higher recurrence rates of HPV-related cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and invasive cervical cancer, underscoring the importance of more frequent cervical screening in HIV-positive women.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Molluscum contagiosum, a viral skin infection that can affect the genital area, is characterized by which classic lesion appearance?
o: Painful vesicles on an erythematous base
A single painless, indurated ulcer
Small, dome-shaped papules with characteristic central umbilication
Frothy, malodorous discharge without any skin lesion
Diffuse erythema with peau d'orange skin change
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Molluscum contagiosum, caused by a poxvirus, presents with small, firm, dome-shaped, flesh-colored papules with a characteristic central umbilication, which can occur in the genital area when transmitted sexually.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Actinomyces infection is classically associated with which gynecological device when present for a prolonged period?
o: A contraceptive vaginal ring used for less than one month
A cervical cap used for a single cycle
A diaphragm used for a single act of intercourse
A copper intrauterine device used for less than 3 months
A long-standing intrauterine device
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Actinomyces israelii colonization (and rarely invasive actinomycosis) is classically associated with long-term use of an intrauterine device, and its incidental detection on cervical cytology in an asymptomatic woman with an IUD does not necessarily require device removal unless symptomatic infection is present.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Cervical ectropion (eversion), a common benign finding in which columnar epithelium is visible on the exocervix, is most commonly associated with which factor?
o: High estrogen states, such as pregnancy or combined oral contraceptive use
Menopause and low estrogen states as the most common association
Chronic pelvic inflammatory disease as the most common association
Cervical cancer as the most common association
Vulvar lichen sclerosus as the most common association
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Cervical ectropion, where the columnar epithelium of the endocervix everts onto the visible exocervix, is most commonly associated with high estrogen states such as pregnancy, adolescence, or combined oral contraceptive use, and is a benign finding that can sometimes cause postcoital spotting.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Choriocarcinoma, a malignant form of gestational trophoblastic disease, is characterized by which tumor marker used for diagnosis and monitoring?
o: Alpha-fetoprotein as the primary tumor marker
CA-125 as the primary tumor marker for choriocarcinoma
Prostate-specific antigen as the primary tumor marker
Beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (beta-hCG)
Carcinoembryonic antigen as the primary tumor marker
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: Choriocarcinoma, like other forms of gestational trophoblastic disease, secretes beta-human chorionic gonadotropin, which serves as a highly sensitive tumor marker for diagnosis, monitoring treatment response, and detecting recurrence.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: A partial hydatidiform mole, unlike a complete mole, is characterized by which genetic and pathological feature?
o: Triploidy, typically from fertilization of a normal ovum by two sperm, with some fetal tissue often present
A purely paternal diploid genome with complete absence of any fetal tissue
A purely maternal diploid genome with a normal, viable fetus
Identical genetic and pathological features to a complete mole in every respect
Complete absence of any trophoblastic proliferation
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: A partial hydatidiform mole typically results from triploidy, most often from fertilization of a normal ovum by two sperm (or a diploid sperm), and unlike a complete mole, often shows some identifiable fetal or embryonic tissue alongside abnormal trophoblastic proliferation.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.s: Human papillomavirus vaccination is recommended for both boys and girls in part because HPV infection is also associated with which cancer in men?
o: Testicular seminoma as the primary HPV-associated male cancer
Prostate adenocarcinoma as the primary HPV-associated male cancer
Renal cell carcinoma as the primary HPV-associated male cancer
Bladder urothelial carcinoma as the primary HPV-associated male cancer
Oropharyngeal and anal squamous cell carcinoma
obstetrics-and-gynecology/gynecological-.e: HPV infection in men is associated with oropharyngeal and anal squamous cell carcinoma, as well as genital warts and penile cancer, providing part of the rationale for universal HPV vaccination of both sexes.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.s: Infertility is generally defined as the inability to conceive after how long of regular, unprotected intercourse in a woman under 35 years of age?
o: 12 months
1 month
3 months
5 years
10 years
obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.e: Infertility is generally defined as the failure to achieve pregnancy after 12 months of regular, unprotected intercourse in women under 35 years of age, with earlier evaluation (after 6 months) often recommended for women 35 and older.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.s: Which single investigation is most commonly used as an initial assessment of tubal patency in the infertility workup?
o: Hysterosalpingography
Diagnostic laparoscopy as the first-line test in all cases
Transvaginal ultrasound alone as the definitive test for tubal patency
Endometrial biopsy as the test for tubal patency
Serum progesterone level as the test for tubal patency
obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.e: Hysterosalpingography, involving injection of radiopaque contrast through the cervix with fluoroscopic imaging, is commonly used as an initial, relatively non-invasive assessment of tubal patency and uterine cavity contour in the infertility workup.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.s: A mid-luteal phase serum progesterone level is measured in the infertility workup primarily to assess which reproductive function?
o: Ovarian reserve directly, in place of other hormonal markers
Tubal patency
Confirmation of ovulation
Uterine cavity contour
Semen quality
obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.e: A mid-luteal phase (approximately 7 days after presumed ovulation) serum progesterone level is used to confirm that ovulation has occurred, as progesterone rises significantly following ovulation due to corpus luteum formation.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.s: Anti-Mullerian hormone, a marker increasingly used to assess ovarian reserve, is produced by which ovarian structure?
o: The corpus luteum exclusively
Granulosa cells of small growing (preantral and small antral) follicles
The ovarian surface epithelium exclusively
Theca cells exclusively
The primary oocyte itself, independent of any surrounding cells
obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.e: Anti-Mullerian hormone is produced by granulosa cells of small growing ovarian follicles and correlates with the size of the remaining ovarian follicular pool, making it a useful marker of ovarian reserve that remains relatively stable throughout the menstrual cycle.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.s: A semen analysis, a key component of the male infertility evaluation, typically assesses which parameters?
o: Serum testosterone level exclusively, without any direct semen assessment
Prostate-specific antigen level exclusively
Testicular volume by ultrasound exclusively, without any semen assessment
Serum FSH level exclusively, without any direct semen assessment
Sperm concentration, motility, and morphology
obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.e: Semen analysis evaluates key parameters including sperm concentration (count), motility, and morphology, alongside volume and other characteristics, providing essential information in the evaluation of male factor infertility.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.s: Clomiphene citrate, commonly used to induce ovulation in anovulatory infertility, acts primarily by which mechanism?
o: Directly stimulating the ovary to release an oocyte, bypassing the hypothalamic-pituitary axis entirely
Suppressing gonadotropin-releasing hormone secretion to prevent ovulation
Blocking estrogen receptors at the hypothalamus, reducing negative feedback and increasing gonadotropin release
Directly increasing progesterone production by the corpus luteum
Acting as a direct exogenous source of follicle-stimulating hormone
obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.e: Clomiphene citrate is a selective estrogen receptor modulator that blocks estrogen receptors at the hypothalamus, reducing negative feedback inhibition and thereby increasing endogenous gonadotropin-releasing hormone and gonadotropin secretion, stimulating follicular development and ovulation.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.s: In vitro fertilization involves which key sequence of steps?
o: Direct intrauterine insemination of washed sperm without any oocyte retrieval
Controlled ovarian stimulation, oocyte retrieval, fertilization outside the body, and embryo transfer into the uterus
Surgical correction of tubal blockage as the primary intervention
Administration of clomiphene citrate alone, without any additional procedures
Donation of an entire ovary for transplantation
obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.e: In vitro fertilization involves controlled ovarian stimulation to produce multiple mature oocytes, transvaginal ultrasound-guided oocyte retrieval, fertilization of the oocytes with sperm outside the body (in vitro), and subsequent transfer of resulting embryo(s) into the uterine cavity.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.s: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome, a recognized complication of assisted reproductive technology, results from which underlying process?
o: Insufficient ovarian response to gonadotropin stimulation
A direct toxic effect of the embryo transfer catheter on the ovary
Chronic, longstanding untreated polycystic ovary syndrome unrelated to any treatment
Complete ovarian failure following stimulation
Excessive ovarian response to gonadotropin stimulation, causing increased vascular permeability and fluid shifts
obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.e: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome results from an excessive ovarian response to gonadotropin stimulation, with markedly enlarged ovaries and increased vascular permeability (mediated in part by vascular endothelial growth factor) causing fluid shifts into the peritoneal and pleural spaces, in severe cases leading to significant morbidity.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.s: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection, a technique used within in vitro fertilization, is particularly indicated for which type of infertility?
o: Severe male factor infertility, including very low sperm count or poor motility
Isolated tubal factor infertility with normal semen parameters
Isolated ovulatory dysfunction with normal semen parameters
Isolated uterine anomalies with normal semen parameters
Age-related decline in ovarian reserve with normal semen parameters
obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.e: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection, involving direct injection of a single sperm into an oocyte, is particularly indicated for severe male factor infertility (very low sperm count, poor motility, or abnormal morphology), bypassing the need for sperm to penetrate the oocyte unassisted.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.s: Combined oral contraceptive pills primarily prevent pregnancy through which mechanism?
o: Direct spermicidal action within the vagina
Suppression of ovulation via negative feedback inhibition of gonadotropin release
Physical blockage of the fallopian tubes
Induction of early endometrial shedding before implantation is possible in all cycles
Direct destruction of oocytes within the ovary
obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.e: Combined oral contraceptive pills primarily prevent pregnancy by suppressing ovulation through negative feedback inhibition of gonadotropin-releasing hormone and gonadotropin secretion, with additional contraceptive effects from thickened cervical mucus and altered endometrial receptivity.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.s: Which contraceptive method provides the longest duration of action from a single administration, among common reversible methods?
o: A copper intrauterine device (effective for up to 10 years or more)
The combined oral contraceptive pill (requiring daily dosing)
The contraceptive patch (requiring weekly replacement)
The vaginal ring (requiring monthly replacement)
Emergency contraception (a single-use method for post-coital prevention)
obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.e: A copper intrauterine device provides highly effective, long-acting reversible contraception for up to 10 years or more from a single insertion, making it one of the longest-duration reversible contraceptive methods available.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.s: The copper intrauterine device prevents pregnancy primarily through which mechanism?
o: Suppression of ovulation, similarly to combined oral contraceptives
Systemic hormonal suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis
Physical occlusion of the fallopian tubes
Induction of permanent endometrial atrophy preventing any future fertility
A local inflammatory reaction in the endometrium that is toxic to sperm and ova, impairing fertilization
obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.e: The copper intrauterine device works primarily through a local, sterile inflammatory reaction within the endometrial cavity that is toxic to sperm and ova, impairing sperm motility and function and preventing fertilization, without suppressing ovulation.

obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.s: Progestin-only contraceptive methods (e.g., the mini-pill, implant, or injectable) are particularly useful for women with which contraindication to estrogen-containing methods?
o: A history of venous thromboembolism or migraine with aura
A history of iron deficiency anemia
A history of well-controlled hypothyroidism
A history of seasonal allergies
A history of resolved gestational diabetes
obstetrics-and-gynecology/infertility-an.e: Progestin-only contraceptive methods avoid the estrogen-related increased risk of venous thromboembolism and are therefore preferred for women with a history of venous thromboembolism, migraine with aura, or other estrogen contraindications.
